title: Staff Software Engineer | Developer Experience
description:
Meet DeepL

DeepL is a global AI product and research company focused on building secure, intelligent solutions to complex business problems. Over 200,000 business customers and millions of individuals across 228 global markets today trust DeepL's Language AI platform for human-like translation, improved writing and real-time voice translation.
Founded in 2017 by CEO Jaroslaw “Jarek” Kutylowski, DeepL now has around 1,000 passionate employees and is supported by world-renowned investors including Benchmark, IVP, and Index Ventures.

Our goal is to become the global leader in trusted, intelligent AI technology, building products that drive better communication, foster connections, and create a meaningful impact. To achieve this, we need talented people like you to join our journey. If you’re ready to shape the future of AI and grow your career in a fast-moving, purpose-driven environment, DeepL is your next destination.

What sets us apart

What sets us apart is our blend of cutting-edge AI technology, meaningful work, and a culture where people truly thrive. We’re a team of innovators, researchers, and creators driven by a shared purpose to unlock human potential by making work simpler, smarter, and more connected.

When we share what it’s like to work at DeepL, the reactions are overwhelmingly positive. This might be because of our technology that helps millions of people and businesses communicate and work better every day, or because of the trust, curiosity, and care that shape our culture.

What we know for sure is this: being part of DeepL means joining a team dedicated to innovation, growth, and well-being. Discover more about life at DeepL onLinkedIn,Instagram, and our Blog.

Meet the team behind this journey

You will join the Developer Experience track, whose customers are DeepL's own engineers. Every change that reaches our products, from a research prototype to a production release, travels through the platform, pipelines and workflows this track owns. Our job is to make that journey fast, safe and obvious, so that engineers spend their time on the problems only they can solve.

That ownership runs the full width of the developer's day. It covers the foundation: source control, the CI and CD fleet that runs every pipeline across Kubernetes, macOS and Windows, build and dependency caching, and the artifact and package registries that hold what we ship. Having recently moved our source and CI onto GitLab SaaS, we are now shaping what a genuinely self-service platform looks like on top of it.

It also covers everything an engineer actually touches: our internal developer portal and service catalogue in Backstage, the Golden Path templates and release automation that make the right thing the easy thing, automated guardrails for security and production readiness, self-service access management, and the AI tooling our engineers use every day, including AI-assisted code review. We measure whether any of it is working, through developer surveys and delivery metrics.

We treat developer experience as a product, not a support function. We are opinionated about paved roads, allergic to mandates without migration paths, and increasingly focused on a question the whole industry is still answering: what does an engineering organisation look like when AI is a first-class part of how software gets built?

Your responsibilities

  • Own technical direction for a significant part of the Developer Experience mandate. Identify where the biggest friction sits for our engineers, form a clear position on how to remove it, and see that work through to adoption.

  • Lead initiatives that lift developer productivity across multiple engineering teams, by understanding and improving processes and tooling, and by drawing on both established software engineering practice and AI capability.

  • Design and build the workflows and tooling that carry a change through the software development lifecycle, from local development through review to release.

  • Lead our work on AI across that lifecycle. Evaluate what genuinely helps, build the guardrails that make it safe and useful at our scale, and be candid about what does not work.

  • Treat internal developers as customers and grow a community around developer experience. Talk to them, watch where they struggle, and let evidence decide what to build and whether it landed, whether that evidence is survey data, delivery metrics or support load. Empower product teams to own their delivery journey, and turn consensus across engineering into shipped change. Much of the work at this level is influence without authority.

  • Define standards that hold across the track and drive migrations to them, bringing teams along with a working path rather than a deadline.

  • Mentor engineers across the track and raise the technical bar of the group, through design reviews, architecture decisions and the everyday habits that keep systems maintainable.

  • Share in operating what we build, including a sustainable on call rotation for the services and tooling other teams rely on.

Qualities we look for

  • A software engineering background, in any language, with real depth in at least one. We genuinely do not mind which: C#, Go, TypeScript and Python are all well represented here. We care that you can build software other engineers rely on, and that you can read your way into an unfamiliar codebase.

  • Time in a product team, shipping to external customers. The best developer experience work comes from people who have personally felt the pipeline they are now redesigning, and who know what a product team is actually optimising for.

  • Genuine passion for developer experience. Build systems, CI and CD, internal platforms, release engineering, and the texture of what makes a codebase pleasant or miserable to work in. This is a role for someone who finds this intrinsically interesting, not a stepping stone.

  • Enthusiasm for figuring out where AI creates real leverage in how software gets built, a willingness to run experiments that fail, and enough scepticism to tell the difference between a genuine improvement and a demo.

  • A track record of technical ownership spanning several teams. You create clarity where a mandate crosses team boundaries, hold clear positions, change them on evidence, and carry other engineers with you.

  • The judgement to trade the ideal solution for one you can ship and iterate on, and the tenacity to keep going. Changing how an engineering organisation works is a long game, and adoption is the hard part.

You would get bonus points for

  • Measuring developer productivity credibly, through DORA, developer surveys, or your own defensible approach.

  • Having built or operated AI-assisted developer tooling: code review, agents, MCP servers, or evaluation of any of the above.

  • Experience building an internal developer platform or portal, especially with Backstage.

  • Community building you can point to. Open source maintainership, a guild or community of practice, developer advocacy, or any place you have grown adoption and ownership rather than mandated it.

  • GitLab or comparable CI and CD at scale, and build system work on large polyglot codebases. Runner fleets, pipeline performance, caching and artifacts, and compile and test time optimisation.

What we offer

  • Diverse and internationally distributed team: joining our team means becoming part of a large, global community with people of more than 90 nationalities. We're more than just colleagues; we're a group of professionals with a shared mission to connect diverse cultures. Our global presence is growing–we've doubled in size nearly every year, with our employees based in the UK, Germany, the Netherlands, Poland, the US, and Japan, and we continue to expand our network.

  • Open communication, regular feedback: as a language-focused company, we value the importance of clear, honest communication. We value smooth collaboration, direct and actionable feedback, and believe that leading with empathy and growth mindset makes us better together.

  • Hybrid work, flexible hours: we offer a hybrid work schedule, with team members coming into the office twice a week. This allows you to engage directly with your team and experience the unique energy of our workspace, while still enjoying the flexibility and comfort of working from home. With flexible working hours and trust in your productivity, we are in sync with your team’s general locations and time zones to foster effective and seamless collaboration.

  • Virtual Shares - An ownership mindset in every role. We believe everyone should share in our success, and that’s why every employee receives Virtual Shares, linking your contribution directly to DeepL’s growth and rewarding you with a stake in our future.

  • Regular in-person team events: we bond over vibrant events that are as unique as our team, from local team and business unit gatherings, to new-joiner onboardings, to company-wide events that bring us all together–literally.

  • Monthly full-day hacking sessions: every month, we have Hack Fridays, where you can spend your time diving into a project you're passionate about and get the opportunity to work with other teams–we value your initiatives, impact, and creativity.

  • 30 days of annual leave: we value your peace of mind. With 30 days off (excluding public holidays) and access to mental health resources, we make sure you're as strong mentally as you are professionally.

  • Competitive benefits: just as our team spans the globe, so does our benefits package. We've crafted it to reflect the diversity of our team and tailored it to align with your unique location, to ensure you feel supported every step of the way.

If this role and our mission resonate with you, but you're hesitant because you don't check all the boxes, don't let that hold you back. At DeepL, it's all about the value you bring and the growth we can foster together. Go ahead, apply—let's discover your potential together. We can't wait to meet you!

We are an equal opportunity employer

You are welcome at DeepL for who you are - we appreciate authenticity here. Our product is for everyone, and so is our workplace. The more voices we have represented and amplified in our business, the more we will all succeed, contribute, and think forward! So bring us your personal experience, your perspectives, and your background. It’s in our diversity that we will find the power to break down language barriers in the world.

  • Establish clear guardrails, security standards, and production pathways to turn quick, hacky AI prototypes into secure, scalable, and well-architected systems

  • Engage directly with both technical and non-technical stakeholders across business units to help map out fuzzy operational problems, understand pain points, and design practical AI-augmented workflows

  • Collaborate closely with the Data team to ensure data flows securely and effectively into front-facing AI tools and applications

title: Senior Product Data Analyst - Consumer Growth
description:
About the team

SumUp is best known for helping small businesses get paid — our Consumer tribe builds the other half of that story. We make SumUp Consumer, the wallet app that lets everyday consumers pay SumUp merchants with a tap, send money to friends, track their spending and earn loyalty rewards along the way.

As we grow SumUp Consumer across new markets and features, we need sharp, reliable insight into how people discover, adopt and use the product — and how that behaviour translates into sustainable commercial growth. This includes understanding our acquisition funnel, improving activation and conversion, increasing customer value, and reducing churn.

We're looking for a Product Data Analyst to join the Consumer tribe and become the analytical partner for SumUp Consumer. You'll work closely with Product Managers, Designers and Engineers, alongside our Analytics Engineering team, to understand customer behaviour, shape product strategy, and connect product performance to business outcomes.

You'll help answer questions such as:

  • Which acquisition channels and customer segments generate the strongest long-term value?
  • Where do customers drop out of the journey from acquisition to activation?
  • What drives repeat usage, retention and churn?
  • Which product changes improve conversion, customer value or commercial performance?
  • How should we prioritise product investments across markets and customer segments?

If you're motivated by meaningful analytical work, enjoy translating complexity into clarity, and want to see your insights directly influence both product decisions and commercial outcomes, this role is for you.

What you'll do

  • Analyse customer behaviour and product performance across the full consumer lifecycle — from acquisition and activation through engagement, retention, churn and reactivation.
  • Identify opportunities to improve conversion, customer value and sustainable growth using funnel analysis, cohort analysis, segmentation and behavioural analytics.
  • Collaborate closely with Product Managers, Designers, Engineers and Data teams to ensure decisions are grounded in robust analysis, customer insight and commercial understanding.
  • Evaluate the performance of customer segments, markets, channels and product journeys, helping the team understand where growth opportunities and commercial trade-offs exist.
  • Support decisions that improve key business outcomes, such as activation, conversion, repeat usage, retention, churn, customer lifetime value and revenue-related metrics.
  • Conduct exploratory analysis to answer product and business questions, translating complex data into clear, commercially relevant recommendations.
  • Define, monitor and communicate core SumUp Consumer KPIs, covering acquisition, activation, engagement, conversion, retention, churn and customer value.
  • Design, execute and analyse A/B tests and product experiments, assessing both customer impact and commercial impact.
  • Build and maintain dashboards and reporting that stakeholders actively use, proactively surfacing trends, anomalies, performance risks and growth opportunities.
  • Help Product Managers assess the expected impact of opportunities and evaluate whether product investments are delivering the intended customer and business outcomes.
  • Partner with Analytics Engineering to ensure KPI definitions, business logic and product instrumentation are accurate, scalable and trusted.
  • Bring a curious eye to AI and machine learning techniques, including LLM-assisted analysis, to speed up insight generation, customer understanding and product measurement.

You'll be great for this role if…

  • You have strong SQL skills and are comfortable querying, analysing and validating data in a cloud data warehouse such as Snowflake, BigQuery or similar.
  • You have hands-on experience with product analytics techniques such as funnel analysis, cohort analysis, segmentation and behavioural analysis.
  • You understand the commercial drivers of a digital product, including customer acquisition, conversion, activation, retention, churn and customer lifetime value.
  • You can connect customer behaviour and product performance to business outcomes, and use data to identify growth opportunities and inform prioritisation.
  • You've worked on A/B tests or product experiments, with a solid grounding in the statistics behind them.
  • You're proficient in a visualisation tool such as Looker, Tableau or Power BI, with a track record of building dashboards that stakeholders actually use.
  • You can translate ambiguous product or business questions into structured analysis, and explain findings clearly to technical and non-technical audiences alike.
  • You're comfortable assessing trade-offs, challenging assumptions and making recommendations based on evidence.
  • You're curious about how AI and emerging techniques can improve product measurement, experimentation, customer understanding and commercial decision-making.
  • You're comfortable managing multiple workstreams and stakeholders, with strong prioritisation and a proactive communication style.

This role does not support Visa sponsorship and candidates must have the right to work in the UK.

Why you should join SumUp

🌎 Opportunity to work with a truly global, multicultural team from our central London Bridge location, wrapped in historic charm and modern flair. This involves an office-first setup

🌈 Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion: be part of a workplace that values and promotes diversity, fostering an inclusive environment where everyone's perspectives are respected and embraced

🚀 Enrolment onto our Virtual Stock Option programme: you will own a stake in SumUp's future success

🏖 Generous time off: enjoy 28 days of paid leave, plus bank holidays and special leaves

📚 A dedicated annual L&D budget for attending conferences and/or advancing your career through further education

🏥 Health matters: private health insurance, including optical and dental

🚗 Life made easier: salary-sacrifice commuter benefits via Gogeta

💼 Financial security: retirement scheme (SumUp matches 7% when you contribute 5%)

🛡 Peace of mind: life insurance from MetLife for 2× your salary

🌴 Break4me: 1-month sabbatical after 3 years of service

🔗 Referral Bonus: earn additional rewards by referring talented individuals to join the SumUp team

About SumUp

Be empowered to do more that matters.

At SumUp, we're on a mission to empower small businesses across the globe by providing simple and affordable tools that allow them to thrive. Today, over 4 million businesses in 37 markets rely on SumUp as their financial partner to manage payments, finance and customer relationships.

Our commitment to small businesses is reflected in our diverse team of over 3,000 SumUppers from over 90 nationalities, united by global collaboration and an innovative mindset. Our core values lay the foundation for who we are and what we stand for, shaping our work culture and driving our success. We foster inclusivity and a continuous learning culture, providing a safe space for personal and professional growth. Our differences make us unique and strong as we strive to create an environment where everyone belongs and feels supported, no matter how they identify.

SumUp is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity employer, actively seeking and embracing diversity in our workforce. We don't make hiring or employment decisions based on race, colour, religion or religious belief, ethnic or national origin, nationality, sex, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, disability, age or any other basis protected by applicable laws or prohibited by company policy. Our commitment extends beyond recruitment to creating a safe and respectful workplace where harassment of any form is strictly prohibited. title: Staff AI Deployment Strategist - UK & Nordics
description:
About Mistral

Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems—across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector—co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms.

We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited.

The Role

 

As Staff AI Deployment Strategist, you will shape how some of the most ambitious enterprises in the UK & Nordics region adopt frontier AI at scale.

This is a senior, high-impact role at the intersection of strategy, technology, and execution. You will work directly on Mistral’s most strategic opportunities and largest deliveries, helping customers move from ambition to measurable business outcomes. You will frame complex AI transformation programs, turn executive priorities into actionable roadmaps, and ensure that Mistral delivers systems that are valuable, scalable, and trusted.

You will also act as a senior sponsor on our most critical customer programs, bringing judgment, structure, and delivery excellence to high-stakes engagements. Your mandate is to raise the ambition and quality of AI adoption: helping customers identify where AI can create step-change value, making the right trade-offs, and ensuring that execution matches the strategic promise.

This role is ideal for an experienced strategy consultant, transformation leader, or senior operator who wants to move from advising on change to building it directly with frontier AI technology.

 

What You Will Do

  • Shape high-impact AI transformations

    • Partner closely with Mistral’s Sales leadership in the UK & Nordics to qualify opportunities, align on account strategy, and drive executive engagement.

    • Work with senior customer stakeholders to identify where frontier AI can create material business value.

    • Structure complex opportunities into clear, credible, and executable transformation programs.

    • Translate strategic ambition into delivery roadmaps, success metrics, and operating plans.

    • Help customers make the right trade-offs between ambition, feasibility, speed, and long-term scalability.

  • Sponsor Mistral’s most strategic deliveries

    • Act as a senior sponsor on the largest and most complex customer programs, primarily in the UK & Nordics and potentially cross-region as priorities evolve.

    • Ensure delivery quality, executive alignment, and measurable business impact.

    • Anticipate risks, unblock decisions, and help teams navigate ambiguity in high-stakes environments.

    • Bring senior judgment to moments where scope, resources, timelines, or expected value need to be clarified.

  • Build repeatable deployment excellence

    • Turn lessons from strategic engagements into reusable approaches, playbooks, and patterns.

    • Raise the bar for how AI programs are qualified, framed, delivered, and scaled.

    • Act as a senior relay for the Solutions organization in the region, helping teams adopt shared best practices, adapt them thoughtfully to local market specificities when needed, and strengthen the quality of execution.

    • Work hand in hand with Solutions leadership to connect customer realities, delivery patterns, and field feedback into practical ways of improving how Mistral deploys AI.

    • Help codify what great enterprise AI deployment looks like across industries and use cases.

    • Contribute to a Solutions culture that combines strategic clarity, technical depth, and strong execution.

  • Develop and multiply senior DS impact

    • Coach Deployment Strategists on strategic problem-solving, executive communication, and delivery leadership.

    • Help teams raise the quality of their work on the highest-impact opportunities.

    • Identify capability gaps and contribute to hiring, staffing, and development priorities.

    • Act as a force multiplier across accounts, teams, and regions where your experience can have the highest leverage.

 
 

What We're Looking For

 

You are a senior, highly capable professional with strong executive presence, excellent business judgment, and a track record of leading complex strategic or transformation work.

Typical indicators we’re looking for include:

  • 8–10+ years of professional experience in strategy consulting, digital transformation, AI, enterprise technology, or a similarly demanding environment.

  • Experience operating at Partner, Principal, Engagement Manager, Director, or equivalent level in a top-tier strategy consulting or transformation context.

  • A strong ability to structure ambiguous problems, identify value, and turn strategy into execution.

  • Experience leading large accounts, complex programs, or senior customer relationships.

  • The credibility to engage with executives and C-level stakeholders on business priorities, trade-offs, and impact.

  • Strong analytical and commercial judgment, with the ability to challenge assumptions constructively.

  • Comfort working at the frontier of technology, even when solutions are evolving quickly and the path is not fully defined.

  • A low-ego, high-ownership mindset and a desire to build with customers and teams, not just advise from a distance.

  • Fluency in English; German is a strong plus.

 

Hiring Process

title: Retail Store Operations Manager - Bicester Village
description:
TALA has been on a rocket ship since its founding in 2019 by entrepreneur Grace Beverley. Built on largely organic social, today we are a digital-first, multichannel women’s activewear brand with a multifaceted growth and retention strategy.

Following a £5m fundraise from world-class institutional investors and growing global media attention, TALA is entering an exciting new phase of growth, including the opening of two stores in London.

Now, we’re taking TALA beyond London, and Bicester Village, you’re next.

*This will be for a FTC from November 26 to January 27*

Tasks

What you'll be doing

Goods In & Stock Flow

  • Own the end-to-end flow of stock from delivery to shop floor, taking full accountability for backroom performance.
  • Plan and manage delivery days around Bicester Village's service yard access and delivery windows, ensuring the team is resourced and ready ahead of every drop.
  • Receive, check and book in all deliveries accurately and on the day of arrival, escalating discrepancies, shortages and damages to Logistics within agreed timeframes.
  • Set and hold a clear delivery-to-floor turnaround standard

Processing, Pricing & Retail Ready

  • Own the "retail ready" standard end to end: steamed, sized, hung or folded, correctly hangered, security tagged, ticketed and floor-ready before it leaves the stockroom.
  • Manage the outlet pricing and ticketing process with total accuracy, ensuring every unit carries the correct price and any was/now ticketing is applied in line with brand and regulatory guidelines.
  • Execute promotional changes, markdowns and price changes to deadline, including overnight or pre-trade implementation where needed.
  • Build simple, repeatable processing routines and workstation set-ups that let the team move at volume without losing accuracy.
  • Track and improve processing productivity, using units-per-hour measures to plan labour and forecast the resource needed for peak drops.

Stock Accuracy & Inventory Integrity

  • Be the store's owner of stock file accuracy, treating the integrity of our data as a core deliverable rather than an admin task.
  • Run a disciplined cycle counting programme across the store, prioritising high-value, high-volume and known problem lines.
  • Investigate and resolve negative stock, unknown barcodes, duplicate barcodes and mis-scanning patterns, feeding root causes back to HQ rather than simply correcting the symptom.
  • Lead the store's preparation for and execution of full stocktakes, including pre-count housekeeping, team briefing, counting discipline and post-count exception resolution.
  • Own shrinkage performance for the store alongside the Store Manager, identifying loss drivers and putting practical controls in place.

Replenishment & Trading Support

  • Ensure the shop floor is fully sized and replenished at open, through the day and at close, so we never lose a sale to a size sitting in a box.
  • Partner with the Store Manager on floor moves, launches and campaign execution, making sure stock is available in the right quantity at the right moment.
  • Provide the Store Manager and Merchandising with clear, timely feedback on size and line performance, sell-through, over-stocks and gaps.
  • Support omnichannel fulfilment activity in store, including click and collect and any in-store fulfilment we introduce, to the service levels we set.

Backroom Management & Space

  • Design and maintain a stockroom layout that works at volume: logical, labelled, densely but safely stored, and quick to pick from.
  • Manage stockroom capacity actively, flagging space risk ahead of major intakes and working with HQ on solutions before it becomes a trading problem.
  • Own backroom housekeeping, packaging management, waste and recycling, in line with TALA's sustainability commitments.
  • Keep all equipment, consumables and ticketing supplies stocked and functioning.

Team Leadership

  • Lead, coach and develop the stockroom team, building a small operation that takes genuine pride in pace, accuracy and standards.
  • Own rota planning for the backroom team, matching labour to the delivery schedule and trading peaks within payroll budget.
  • Recruit, onboard and train new team members on all BOH processes, and build stockroom capability across the wider store team.
  • Set clear daily targets and priorities, and hold the team to them through visible, on-the-floor leadership.

Compliance, Safety & Deputising

  • Ensure health and safety compliance across all back of house areas, including manual handling, safe stacking, fire exits and equipment checks, with regular audits and documented training.
  • Embed loss prevention procedures across goods in, stockroom and waste routines.
  • Ensure the store meets all Bicester Village centre operating standards and requirements.
  • Act as a key holder, opening and closing the store, and deputise for the Store Manager in their absence - including on trade, service and team decisions.

Requirements

About you:

  • Experience in a retail environment, preferably in fashion, activewear, or wellness—but above all, a genuine passion for these areas is a must.
  • Exceptional communication and interpersonal skills, allowing you to connect effortlessly with customers and inspire your team.
  • A natural problem-solver—proactive, quick to learn, and able to thrive both independently and as part of a dynamic team.
  • Strong visual merchandising instincts, with a keen eye for detail to keep the store looking stylish and on-brand at all times.
  • Excellent multitasking skills, balancing customer service, sales, and store operations seamlessly in a fast-paced environment.
  • Fluent in English (reading, writing, and speaking) to ensure clear and engaging customer interactions.
  • Passionate about building customer relationships, from discussing upcoming collections to gathering customer insights that foster long-term loyalty.

Benefits

Some of our core benefits include:

  • 28 days holiday a year inclusive of bank holidays
  • You'll be automatically enrolled in our company pension scheme with Aviva
  • Employee discount after probation period
  • Clothing allowance spending gift
  • TALA Uniform

About us

TALA is an activewear brand built to actively solve problems without creating new ones for people, the planet, or anyone else. Every collection prioritises functionality and thoughtful design, combining premium fabrics with multi-way versatility and flattering fits that deliver maximum impact with minimal effort. Each piece is crafted with attention to detail, ensuring women can look and feel their best with ease.

When founder Grace Beverley shifted from fast fashion to more sustainable options in her everyday clothing, she found a host of responsibly made options in every category other than activewear. Founding TALA in 2019, the proud female-led brand is on a mission to make consciously made active and off-duty styles accessible and inclusive without sacrificing performance or fit.

Read about TALA's people, purpose and product work here.

title: Product & Business Analyst
description:
Launch your product career at Europe's leading music education platform

Matchspace Music is Europe's leading music education platform. We help thousands of music teachers build sustainable careers from teaching, and we are scaling fast across international markets. You will work directly with our VP Product.

This is a role for someone hungry. You want to see how a product is discovered, specified, built, shipped, measured and improved, and you want to be hands-on across the whole cycle. Everything we build follows one cycle: build, measure, learn, repeat. We are looking for a sharp analytical mind that is also creative in solving problems and providing fresh insights. In return you get a front-row seat in building AI-powered platforms, an AI-first way of working, and high visibility to the leadership team as we grow internationally.

Tasks

  • Feature conceptualization. Turn evidence into product ideas. You will run the full loop, from insight, to concept and options, to a sprint-ready story, and back to the data to see whether it worked.
  • Requirements engineering. Turn customer insights and support feedback into clear, buildable user stories with business context, acceptance criteria and edge cases. Own the qualification funnel so nothing rots and no ticket enters a sprint under-specified.
  • Sprint operations. Run backlog hygiene, standup and review mechanics, dependency flags and blocker tracking with our development team, so decisions get made once and stay made.
  • UAT, QA and testing. Own regression and release testing. Reproduce defects properly, keep the bug board honest, and support UAT and end-to-end dry runs.
  • Analytics and performance measurement. Own recurring KPI reporting across our tool stack, close measurement gaps, and turn funnel and cohort data into insight the team acts on. Every feature we ship is measured against the question: did it work? What was the impact?

Requirements

  • A relevant degree in business engineering, IT, information systems, digital business administration, or a related field, whether ongoing or recently completed.
  • Analytical and creative. You enjoy digging into data to find the real problem, and you are creative about how to solve it. Build-measure-learn is how you already think.
  • Structured and detail oriented. You find clean documentation and reproducible analysis satisfying, not tedious.
  • Comfortable with data. Excel/Sheets at a solid level, able to read dashboards, willing to learn fast
  • Comfortable and confident with software development technicalities, with viewing software code and understanding code with the help of AI
  • Proficient in German (min. B2) and English (C1). You can write a requirement someone else can build from. Your main operating language is English. German is essential for our Swiss home market.
  • Already using AI tools in your daily productivity workflow and genuinely curious about how software gets built.
  • Self-managing in a fast-moving, distributed team.

Nice to have

Agile/Scrum exposure, ticket systems, manual QA or test-case experience, and an interest in music, education or marketplaces.

Benefits

  • Work directly with the VP Product in a dynamic, cross-functional team spanning Product, Marketing and Customer Success.
  • Full end-to-end exposure: discovery, requirements, delivery, release, measurement and growth.
  • A front-row seat at Europe's leading music education platform, with real breadth across very different product challenges.
  • A modern, AI-first working culture.
  • A high-visibility talent role with direct exposure to the leadership team and an attractive international career trajectory as we scale.

We run a short, structured screening built around real examples of your work and how you think. Tell us who you are, why this role, and when you can start. We will take it from there.
